scenario.description: An underwriting manager must decide whether to issue a standby letter of credit for a construction contractor and finalize its amount, margin, expiry, draw-notice terms, sanctions controls, and message format, with input from risk, compliance, operations, and relationship coverage.

shared_context.S1: The bank has received a request for a standby letter of credit with a face amount of $2,400,000 for a construction contractor's performance obligation.
shared_context.S2: The request currently describes a twelve-month instrument with no specified cash margin, draw-notice period, or message-format requirements.
shared_context.S3: Maya makes the binding underwriting decision and sets the issuance conditions.
shared_context.S4: Under the bank's normal issuance process, Maya conducts a final round-robin check with credit risk, financial crime compliance, trade operations, and relationship coverage before recording the decision.

PF1.text: Jonas completed a risk review this morning showing that the contractor's existing contingent obligations trigger the bank's policy cap. For this request, the cap requires reducing the standby face amount to exactly $1,800,000 and blocking exactly $450,000 in cash margin, which is 25% of the reduced face amount, in a pledged account. The review is not yet attached to the underwriting file.

PF2.text: Elena received a compliance memo this morning confirming that the beneficiary's state-ownership structure requires enhanced sanctions screening before issuance and quarterly screening thereafter; she has not yet updated the transaction checklist.

PF3.text: Ravi found while testing the draft instruction this week that this advising bank can authenticate the instrument only as an MT760 containing the project reference in field 77C; trade operations will reject any other format, but the requirement is not yet recorded in the deal ticket.

PF4.text: Clara received the signed underlying contract yesterday confirming that the standby must expire exactly 300 days after issuance and that any draw request requires 10 business days' advance notice; she has not yet circulated the relevant contract page.

acceptance_conditions: The standby must be issued with a face amount exactly $1,800,000 and cash margin exactly $450,000.
Enhanced sanctions screening must occur before issuance and quarterly thereafter.
The standby must use an MT760 message with the project reference in field 77C.
The standby must expire after exactly 300 days and require 10 business days' advance notice for a draw.
The settlement must include commitments for the blocked cash margin, sanctions-screening schedule, and authenticated MT760 preparation.

content_checks.C7: any('margin' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments) and any('sanctions' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments) and any('MT760' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The request proposes $2,400,000 with no margin; PF1 changes face_amount_usd to exactly $1,800,000 and cash_margin_usd to exactly $450,000 under the contingent-obligation cap.
The shared request has no financial-crime control, while PF2 changes the settlement to require screening before issue and quarterly screening commitments.

The shared request specifies no transmission format, while PF3 changes swift_message_format to MT760, requires the field-77C project reference, and adds a commitment whose detail references MT760 authentication.
The shared request says twelve months with no draw-notice term, while PF4 changes expiry_days to exactly 300 and draw_notice_days to exactly 10.
